newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli planes strike in Lebanon twice on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Israeli planes strike in Lebanon twice on Friday.

text.p: Israeli planes attacked suspected guerrilla targets in south Lebanon twice on Friday, a day after Hizbollah fighters killed three Israeli soldiers, Lebanese security sources said.
They said two planes fired several rockets in each of the raids on ad-Dahr Daidaba ridges south of Syrian-controlled Bekaa valley. There was no immediate word on casualties.
The raids targeted an area where pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas clashed with Israeli forces in south Lebanon on Thursday night, killing three soldiers and wounding seven, according to Israeli army.
In Beirut, Hizbollah leader Sheikh Hassan Nasrallah said: "If Jews do not return to where they came from, the Isalmic guerrillas' fists will throw all invaders and occupiers in the sea."
Nasrallah, a Shi'ite Moslem cleric, was speaking to nearly 75,000 people commemorating the martyrdom in AD 680 of the Prophet Mohammad's grandson Hussein, the third imam of the Shi'ites.

"Any peace process that does not bring all of Palestine back to Palestinians, all of the Golan Heights and all of south Lebanon...is an unfair process and a false one," he said, referring to Arab territories occupied by Israel.
Friday's attacks raised the number of Israeli air raids on Lebanon since the beginning of 1997 to 32.

In Beirut, a Lebanese Army spokesman said that during Thursday night's clash an Israeli helicopter fired a rocket at a Lebanese army position, destroying one armoured vehicle but causing no casualties.
Security sources had said Israeli helicopters twice struck Hizbollah bases just outside the zone after the clash overnight.

The clash brought to nine the number of Israeli soldiers killed and to 35 the number of those wounded in guerrilla attacks in south Lebanon this year. Last year 27 Israeli soldiers were killed in Lebanon.

Hizbollah (Party of God) is fighting to oust some 1,000 Israeli troops and the 3,000-strong allied South Lebanon Army militia holding the south Lebanon zone set up by Israel in 1985 to protect its northern border area from guerrilla raids.
